sang-froid: calm composure and self-control in a difficult or dangerous moment
topgallant: a sail set on a ship's mast above the topsail
starboard: the right-hand side of a ship when facing the front
forecastle: the forward part of a ship's upper deck, where sailors lived
saloon: the main dining and sitting room on a ship
steward: a ship's officer who looks after passengers' food and comfort
tackle: ropes and pulleys used to lift or move heavy objects on a ship
rigging: the system of ropes and chains that supports a ship's masts and sails
screw: a ship's propeller, driven by an engine to move the vessel
coaling: loading coal into a steamship to fuel its engines
three-mast: a sailing ship with three masts carrying square sails
hammer-headed: describing a shark with a wide, flattened head shaped like a hammer
cabin-boy: a young servant who waits on officers and passengers in a ship's cabins
latitude: distance north or south of the equator, measured in degrees
longitude: distance east or west of a fixed meridian, measured in degrees
parallel: an imaginary line of latitude circling the globe east to west
austral: relating to the southern part of the earth or southern hemisphere
circumnavigation: a voyage completely around the world by sea
admiralty: the British government department in charge of the navy
conjecture: an opinion or guess formed without firm proof
conjectures: opinions or guesses formed without firm proof
apprised: informed or made aware of something
inveterate: having a long-established habit that is hard to change
unceremonious: abrupt and without the usual polite formality
implore: to beg someone earnestly and emotionally for something
affirm: to state firmly and confidently that something is true
explicit: stated clearly and directly, leaving no room for doubt
blanks: empty spaces or missing parts in a written document
effaced: rubbed out or worn away so as to be no longer visible
trifling: small and unimportant, not worth serious attention
vexing: annoying and frustrating, causing irritation or worry
foundered: sank or filled with water and became unable to float
wrecked: destroyed or badly damaged, especially by sinking or storm
strait: a narrow stretch of sea connecting two larger bodies of water
bosom: the human chest, regarded as the seat of feeling
rejoined: answered back in reply to something already said
resumed: began again after a pause or interruption
heedless: careless and not paying attention to danger or consequences
brute: a fierce, savage creature, often an animal
valiant: showing great courage and bravery in facing danger
frail: weak and easily broken or damaged
steamed: travelled by steam-powered engine, moving under steam
sea-sickness: nausea and dizziness caused by the rolling motion of a ship
madam: a polite form of address for a woman, used in formal speech
mamma: an old-fashioned affectionate word for mother
precious: very valuable, important, or dearly loved
gravely: in a serious, solemn, or dignified manner
cheerful: happy and bright in mood or appearance
archipelago: a large group or chain of islands clustered together
fathom: a unit of depth at sea, equal to six feet
documents: official written papers that provide evidence or information
fragments: small broken pieces of something larger
